claim: Microsoft shipped an experimental desktop app that watches you perform a task once on screen and reconstructs it into a reusable agent skill — 835 stars and 90 forks in four days.
method: GitHub API: repo created 2026-07-29, 835 stars / 90 forks / 29 open issues as of 2026-08-03; read the open issue list for design constraints.
does: Records a screen work session (optionally with spoken narration), hands it to the GitHub Copilot CLI, and reconstructs it as an intent plus ordered steps, then emits a reusable Skill or Automation.
edge: It inverts how you teach a computer to do a chore: you do it once while it watches, instead of describing or scripting it. The team is also building on-device detection and redaction of sensitive details in the recording.
why_use: The repeated point-and-click chores ordinary people do monthly are exactly the things they can neither script nor describe precisely enough for an agent — but they can always just do them.
gap: No productized way for non-developers to capture and reuse their own workflows as automations; current tool is a developer-facing CLI wrapper.
counter: Microsoft is occupying this directly and has the distribution; a demonstration is also a lossy spec, and the maintainers' own issue tracker notes recordings that miss a step produce a broken skill. Forks are 11% of stars, so this is still developer curiosity rather than proven demand.
differentiator: Treated here as a capability signal, not a business: the opportunity is the consumer wedge — one narrow recurring household chore taught by demonstration, running locally, with the screen recording never leaving the machine. Cold start (Chinese): Xiaohongshu and Bilibili comment sections under 办公自动化 / 重复劳动 tutorials, where people describe the exact monthly ritual they hate. Cold start (English): r/Automate and r/productivity, search 'automate this thing I do every month'.
value: Not a business as shipped; the consumer version would be a paid local desktop app.
risk: Screen recordings are the most sensitive capture surface there is; anything less than fully local processing is unsellable.

zh.claim: 微软放出一个实验性桌面应用：你在屏幕上把一件事做一遍给它看，它就把这段过程还原成「意图＋有序步骤」，再生成一个可复用的 agent 技能——四天 835 星、90 个 fork。
zh.does: 录下你的一段屏幕操作（可以边做边讲），交给 GitHub Copilot CLI 还原成意图和有序步骤，最后输出一个可复用的 Skill 或 Automation。
zh.why_good: 录一段你做事的屏幕操作，AI 还原成意图和步骤，直接生成可复用的技能。
zh.why_use: 普通人每个月都要点一遍的那些重复活儿，恰恰是他们既写不出脚本、也说不清楚给 AI 听的——但他们随时能做一遍。
zh.gap: 它绑死在 Copilot CLI / Microsoft Scout / Copilot Studio 上，以 Electron 源码方式安装，面向的是企业流程作者。普通人那个版本——「做一遍给它看，以后它替你做」，不用配置任何东西——不存在，中文桌面这边更是完全空白。
zh.counter: 微软亲自占着这个位置，分发能力摆在那；而且演示本身是一份有损的说明书，维护者自己的 issue 里就写了：录漏一步，生成的技能就是坏的。fork 只有星数的 11%，目前还是开发者好奇，不算被验证的需求。
zh.differentiator: 这里只当能力信号，不当生意：机会在普通人那一侧——挑一件家里每月重复的窄活，用示范教会它，全程本地跑，屏幕录像一帧都不出这台机器。冷启动（中文）：小红书、B 站「办公自动化」「重复劳动」教程下的评论区，那里的人会把自己最烦的那套月度流程一条条说出来。冷启动（英文）：r/Automate 与 r/productivity 搜 automate this thing I do every month。
zh.value: 就它现在这个形态不是生意；普通人版本会是一次性买断的本地桌面应用。
zh.risk: 屏幕录像是最敏感的一类采集，不做到全程本地就卖不出去。
zh.hook: 每个月都要把同一套繁琐操作点一遍的人——写不出脚本，也说不清楚到让 AI 接手。

hook: The person who clicks through the same tedious ritual every single month and can neither script it nor describe it precisely enough for an AI to take over.
consumer_angle: An ordinary person could record a repetitive task (e.g., data entry, form filling) and turn it into a reusable automation without coding, but the current tool requires CLI and GitHub Copilot setup.
pick_reason: Fresh repo with no verified demand quotes or behavioral evidence; it's a capability signal from Microsoft, not yet a proven pain.
